This study serves to introduce GraftAssure technology to new transplant centers and additionally builds validation data ahead of potential FDA authorization of GraftAssureDx, a kitted version of the company’s clinical assay.

“Here at UCLA, we are always interested in innovative research and therefore, we are participating in the GALACTIC Registry, offered by iMDx,” said UCLA Medical Center’s Dr. Suphamai (Michael) Bunnapradist, MD, MS. “Through this registry we will be able to monitor our patients’ transplanted kidney health, initially with a send-out test and ultimately through in-house testing. It is also very exciting to be the center that enrolled the first patient into this national registry.”

iMDx seeks to deliver a best-in-class molecular diagnostic test kit, to expand and improve testing access for kidney transplant patients, which it anticipates will deliver new value in the estimated $3 billion addressable market for regulated transplant rejection testing.

“We are excited to enroll our first patients in the GALACTIC registry study, the goal of which is to gather performance metrics on GraftAssure to guide biopsy and treatment decisions and congratulations to the UCLA team on enrolling the first participants. UCLA played a foundational role in validating donor-derived cell-free DNA for transplant monitoring, and we are pleased to have them help answer an important clinical question: ‘Can GraftAssure better identify patients whose biopsies will confirm rejection?’” iMDx CEO Josh Riggs said. “GALACTIC aims to demonstrate a positive predictive value above 80%, compared with roughly 50% for current assays. Enrollment also allows more transplant teams to gain firsthand experience with GraftAssure.”

Mr. Riggs continued, “We expect that the data from this registry is what payers and clinicians will look to for real-world evidence, and that it will support payer coverage decisions down the line for the family of products using GraftAssure technology.”
About the GALACTIC Registry Study

The GALACTIC registry study is designed as an observational study of iMDx’s GraftAssure clinical assay in kidney transplant patients to build evidence supporting the previously published Combination Model (CM)-Score and relate it to real-world outcomes.

Additionally, iMDx expects that the study will bridge findings directly from its CLIA lab-run GraftAssureCore test to its GraftAssureDx kitted test in development to be run in-house within transplant centers. The study also has a planned ~3-year follow-up period.
About the CM-Score Used with GraftAssure Technology

Through the launch of its study, iMDx is making progress toward driving clinical adoption and building a scientific case for why digital PCR, which is natively quantitative, can enable use cases for dd-cfDNA testing beyond what is currently on the market. To that end, iMDx established a multi-year target of engaging with 50 U.S. transplant centers to evaluate the clinical utility of its combined score.

This combined score, or CM-score, uses two independent measurements of dd-cfDNA, which the company believes improves the clinical performance of dd-cfDNA compared to currently available options. Specifically, the CM-score mathematically combines the relative (percentage, or %) and absolute (copies per milliliter, or cp/mL) measurements of DNA fragments from the transplanted organ, which in this case is the kidney. This means that there was a tight correlation between the novel GraftAssure CM-score and rejection, and further suggests that the assay is reliably assessing rejection in kidney transplantation versus non-rejection.

The GALACTIC registry is intended to confirm these findings prospectively in real-world clinical use, evaluate their impact on biopsy and immunosuppression management decisions, and generate long-term outcome data. Collection of these data points is intended to support validation as GraftAssure access is expected to expand to new transplant centers upon planned commercialization.
iMDx Transplant Products and Product Candidates in Development

iMDx’s flagship transplant testing technology quantifies a molecular biomarker known as donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA). The Company’s scientists in Germany and the U.S. have played a critical role over the past decade in developing the science that helped establish dd-cfDNA as a trusted biomarker of transplant rejection. iMDx is commercializing this technology using a market-disruptive business strategy. Under the GraftAssure™ brand, iMDx’s transplant diagnostics include the following:
GraftAssureCore – The company’s laboratory-developed test (LDT), currently reimbursed by CMS MolDX at $2,753 per result and performed at iMDx’s CLIA-certified laboratory in Franklin, Tennessee.
GraftAssureIQ – A research-use-only (RUO) kit intended and labeled for non-clinical applications.
GraftAssureDx – The in vitro diagnostic (IVD) kit currently under FDA review for use in clinical decision-making.
